questions.prompt: Shoulder checking means:
questions.explanation: Mirrors leave blind spots beside and behind your vehicle. A shoulder check is a quick look over your shoulder into the blind spot on the side you are moving toward. Key words: "in the direction".

choices.text: Glancing towards the blind spot in the direction the driver intends to move
Glancing into the left outside mirror
Glancing into both the inside and outside mirrors
Glancing into the right outside mirror

questions.prompt: When parking downhill on a two-way road, a driver should:
questions.explanation: When parked downhill, turn the front wheels toward the curb or edge of the road so that if the vehicle rolls, it rolls away from traffic. Always set the parking brake.

choices.text: Turn the front wheels toward the curb or edge of the roadway and set the parking brake
Keep the front wheels positioned straight ahead and set the parking brake
Turn the front wheels away from the curb or edge of the roadway and set the parking brake
Set the parking brake only

questions.prompt: Which statement describes the steps required to reverse in a straight line?
questions.explanation: To reverse in a straight line, place your left hand at the top of the steering wheel, turn your body, and look over your right shoulder through the rear window. Key words: "straight line".

choices.text: Place the left hand at the top of the steering wheel and look over the right shoulder through the rear window
Place the right hand at the top of the steering wheel, look over the left shoulder and use the outside left rear-view mirror
Place the left hand at the bottom of the steering wheel and use both outside mirrors
Keep both hands on the steering wheel and constantly use the inside rear-view mirror for guidance

questions.prompt: When parallel parking, the vehicle's wheels closest to the curb must be within what maximum distance?
questions.explanation: When parallel parked, the wheels nearest the curb must be no more than 50 cm from it. Key words: "maximum distance".

choices.text: 80 cm from the curb
30 cm from the curb
10 cm from the curb
50 cm from the curb

questions.prompt: When completing an angle park, the vehicle's front wheel must be within what maximum distance from the nearest curb?
questions.explanation: When angle parking, the front wheel must be within 50 cm of the curb. Key words: "maximum distance".

choices.text: 100 cm
50 cm
25 cm
75 cm

questions.prompt: Before leaving a parallel parking space on the right side of a road:
questions.explanation: Before pulling out from the right side of the road, signal and shoulder check to the left, because traffic will be coming up on your left.

choices.text: Shoulder check to the right
Turn on the right signal
Shoulder check to the left
Use an arm signal straight out and up

questions.prompt: When a head restraint is raised to the proper position, the centre of the head restraint is:
questions.explanation: A properly adjusted head restraint protects against whiplash. Its centre should be level with the top of your ears, close to the back of your head.

choices.text: Level with the top of the ear
Level with the top of the shoulders
Level with the neck
Level with the top of the head

questions.prompt: Which direction should a vehicle's front wheels be turned when parked uphill on a two-way road with a curb?
questions.explanation: When parked uphill next to a curb, turn the front wheels away from the curb (to the left). If the vehicle rolls back, the front tire will stop against the curb. Key words: "with a curb".

choices.text: Parallel to the curb
To the left
Straight ahead
To the right

questions.prompt: How close can a driver legally park a vehicle to a Stop sign?
questions.explanation: You may not park within 5 metres of a stop sign, so the sign stays visible to other drivers.

choices.text: 1.5 metres
5 metres
10 metres
3 metres

questions.prompt: What minimum distance from a fire hydrant must a vehicle be parked?
questions.explanation: You may not park within 5 metres of a fire hydrant, so firefighters can reach it quickly.

choices.text: 3 metres
4 metres
2 metres
5 metres

questions.prompt: When backing a passenger vehicle to the left, the driver should:
questions.explanation: For Alberta Class 7 (Learner) drivers, backing rules emphasize extreme caution: check surroundings thoroughly (pedestrians, cyclists, vehicles), use mirrors & shoulder checks, look over the shoulder in the direction you're turning (e.g., left shoulder for left turn), steer slowly with two hands (one to steer, one to stabilize), and remember the front swings opposite to the back, requiring quick forward glances. Never reverse into intersections or crosswalks, and be aware that while backup cameras are allowed, you still need to look over your shoulder

choices.text: Look in the inside rea-view mirror and make steering adjustments as necessary
Look over the right shoulder with occasional glances to the front
Look over the left shoulder with occasional glances to the front
Without shoulder checking, use the inside and outside rear view mirrors to ensure the best view to the rear and both sides of the vehicle

questions.prompt: The recommended braking procedure to bring a vehicle to a normal, smooth stop is:
questions.explanation: To bring a vehicle to a smooth, normal stop, you should ease off the gas early, then apply light, gradual pressure to the brake pedal with your right foot, increasing pressure as needed, and finally ease off slightly just before stopping to prevent a jolt, making it a progressive and controlled deceleration.

choices.text: Continually increase brake pressure until the wheels lock
Apply brake pressure, ease off slightly just before the vehicle stops, then re-apply sufficient pressure to stop
Shift the vehicle into neutral and apply steady pressure to the brake pedal until the vehicle comes to a stop
Pump the brake pedal smoothly until the vehicle stops

questions.prompt: In what order should you complete these steps before driving?
questions.explanation: The recommended order is: lock the doors, adjust the seat, adjust the head restraint, adjust the mirrors, then fasten the seat belt. (Driver's Guide p. 44)

choices.text: Lock doors, adjust seat, adjust head restraint, adjust mirrors, fasten seat belt
Fasten seat belt, adjust mirrors, adjust seat, lock doors, adjust head restraint
Adjust mirrors, fasten seat belt, lock doors, adjust seat, adjust head restraint
Adjust seat, fasten seat belt, adjust mirrors, adjust head restraint, lock doors

questions.prompt: How far should you sit from the steering wheel?
questions.explanation: Sit at least 25 centimetres (10 inches) from the steering wheel, the distance recommended by Transport Canada. (Driver's Guide p. 44)

choices.text: At least 10 centimetres
At least 50 centimetres
At least 25 centimetres
As close as possible

questions.prompt: Where should you place your hands on the steering wheel?
questions.explanation: Place your left hand at about 9 o'clock and your right hand at about 3 o'clock. If the wheel design doesn't allow this, use 10 and 2. (Driver's Guide pp. 44, 48)

choices.text: Both hands at 12 o'clock
At about 9 o'clock and 3 o'clock
At about 4 o'clock and 8 o'clock
One hand at the top of the wheel only

questions.prompt: Ideally, how much space should there be between the back of your head and a tilting head restraint?
questions.explanation: If your head restraint tilts, move it forward. Less than 10 centimetres between your head and the restraint is ideal. (Driver's Guide p. 45)

choices.text: Less than 10 centimetres
About 20 centimetres
About 30 centimetres
The space doesn't matter if the height is correct

questions.prompt: How should you adjust your inside rear-view mirror?
questions.explanation: Adjust the inside mirror so the rear window is framed within it, showing as much behind you as possible. (Driver's Guide p. 45)

choices.text: So you can see your own face
So the whole rear window is framed in the mirror
So you can see the back seat passengers
So you can see the lane to your left

questions.prompt: When your outside mirrors are adjusted correctly, you should see:
questions.explanation: Adjust the outside mirrors to reduce blind spots. You should see your own vehicle in a small part of the mirror closest to it. (Driver's Guide p. 45)

choices.text: None of your own vehicle
A small part of your own vehicle
Mostly your own vehicle
Only the road surface

questions.prompt: Your vehicle has air bags. Are you still required to wear a seat belt?
questions.explanation: Yes. You are still required to wear your seat belt in a vehicle with air bags. (Driver's Guide p. 45)

choices.text: No, air bags replace seat belts
Yes, seat belts are required even with air bags
Only on highways
Only in the back seat

questions.prompt: When must you use your signal lights?
questions.explanation: You must signal when moving away from the curb or parking lane, turning left or right, and changing lanes. (Driver's Guide p. 49)

choices.text: Only when turning at intersections
When moving away from the curb, turning, or changing lanes
Only when other vehicles are nearby
Only when changing lanes on a highway

questions.prompt: Which hand signal tells other drivers you are turning right?
questions.explanation: To signal a right turn by hand, bend your left arm upward at the elbow. A straight arm means left, and an arm bent downward means slowing or stopping. (Driver's Guide p. 49)

choices.text: Left arm straight out
Left arm bent downward at the elbow
Right arm out of the passenger window
Left arm bent upward at the elbow

questions.prompt: Which hand signal tells other drivers you are slowing or stopping?
questions.explanation: To signal slowing or stopping by hand, bend your left arm downward at the elbow. (Driver's Guide p. 49)

choices.text: Left arm bent upward at the elbow
Left arm straight out
Left arm bent downward at the elbow
Waving your left arm up and down

questions.prompt: Total stopping distance is made up of:
questions.explanation: Total stopping distance = perception distance + reaction distance + braking distance. (Driver's Guide p. 50)

choices.text: Braking distance only
Perception distance + reaction distance + braking distance
Reaction distance + braking distance
Following distance + braking distance

questions.prompt: About how long does the average driver take to react by moving their foot from the gas to the brake?
questions.explanation: The average reaction time is about three-quarters of a second. Perception takes about another three-quarters of a second. (Driver's Guide pp. 49–50)

choices.text: About one-tenth of a second
About three-quarters of a second
About 3 seconds
About 5 seconds

questions.prompt: How fast should you drive when reversing?
questions.explanation: All reversing must be done at a crawl or slow walking speed. (Driver's Guide p. 51)

choices.text: At 20 km/h
At the same speed as forward driving
As quickly as possible to clear traffic
At a crawl or slow walking speed

questions.prompt: When reversing in a straight line, how much should you turn the steering wheel to correct your direction?
questions.explanation: To correct your steering when reversing straight, turn the wheel no more than a quarter turn. (Driver's Guide p. 51)

choices.text: About a half turn
A full turn
Do not turn the wheel at all
No more than a quarter turn

questions.prompt: When reversing, which way do you turn the steering wheel?
questions.explanation: Turn the wheel in the direction you want the rear of the vehicle to go. The front of the vehicle moves in the opposite direction. (Driver's Guide p. 51)

choices.text: In the opposite direction to where you want the rear to go
In the direction you want the front of the vehicle to go
Keep the wheel straight and let the vehicle find its path
In the direction you want the rear of the vehicle to go

questions.prompt: It is illegal to reverse your vehicle into:
questions.explanation: It is illegal to move your vehicle in reverse into an intersection or a crosswalk. (Driver's Guide p. 51)

choices.text: A driveway
A parking stall
An intersection or a crosswalk
A curb lane

questions.prompt: When reversing out of a driveway onto a street, you should:
questions.explanation: Steer into the nearest traffic lane, then go forward. Don't reverse into a second traffic lane. (Driver's Guide p. 51)

choices.text: Reverse across all lanes to the far side of the road
Reverse into the second lane to leave room for traffic
Reverse quickly so you block traffic for less time
Reverse into the nearest traffic lane, then go forward

questions.prompt: When parking facing uphill on a street without a curb, which way should you turn your front wheels?
questions.explanation: Uphill without a curb, turn the wheels to the right, toward the edge of the road. If the vehicle rolls, it will go off the road and not into traffic. (Driver's Guide p. 55)

choices.text: To the left, toward the centre of the road
Straight ahead
It doesn't matter if the park brake is set
To the right, toward the edge of the road

questions.prompt: How close to a driveway or private road entrance may you park?
questions.explanation: Do not park within one and a half metres (five feet) of access to a garage, private road, or driveway. (Driver's Guide p. 55)

choices.text: No closer than 5 metres
No closer than 50 centimetres
No closer than 10 metres
No closer than 1.5 metres

questions.prompt: How close to the nearest side of a marked crosswalk may you park?
questions.explanation: Do not park within five metres of the nearest side of a marked crosswalk. (Driver's Guide p. 56)

choices.text: No closer than 5 metres
No closer than 1.5 metres
No closer than 15 metres
Right up to the edge of the crosswalk

questions.prompt: When parked on a roadway outside an urban area, your vehicle must be visible from how far away in both directions?
questions.explanation: Outside urban areas, don't park unless there is a clear passage for traffic and your vehicle can be seen for 60 metres in both directions. (Driver's Guide p. 56)

choices.text: 20 metres
60 metres
150 metres
500 metres

questions.prompt: How should you get out of a vehicle parked at the curb on a two-way street?
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors and shoulder check for traffic and cyclists, open the door no wider than necessary, get out quickly, and walk to the rear of the vehicle facing traffic. (Driver's Guide p. 53)

choices.text: Open the door fully and wait for traffic to go around you
Get out quickly without checking, then walk to the front
Check mirrors and shoulder check, open the door only as wide as needed, and walk to the rear facing traffic
Signal left before opening the door

questions.prompt: When leaving a parked car on a hill, you should always:
questions.explanation: Always set the park brake and put the transmission in Park (automatic) or a low gear (manual). (Driver's Guide p. 55)

choices.text: Leave the vehicle in neutral with the wheels straight
Set the park brake only if the hill is steep
Turn on your hazard lights
Set the park brake and put the vehicle in Park or a low gear
